parole.significato: dungeon (immured and very austere prison, often underground)
parole.testo: From Middle High German kerker, kerkære, karkære, from Old High German karkāri, karkari, karkeri, from Proto-West Germanic *karkarī, ultimately from Latin carcer. Doublet of Karzer (“arrest cell, especially at a university”), a later borrowing of the same noun.

parole.significato: mirror (smooth surface, usually made of glass with reflective material painted on the underside, that reflects light)
parole.testo: From Middle High German spiegel, from Old High German spiegal, spēgal, from Proto-West Germanic *spēgl (“mirror”). Cognate with Hunsrik Spieghel.
